newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares end strong despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end strong despite profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking limited gains on Shenzhen's B share index at the close on Friday, but strong buying interest was expected next week for stocks seen as undervalued, brokers said.
The Hong Kong dollar-based B share index surged 7.50 points, or 4.96 percent, to 158.73 as turnover more than doubled for a second day to HK$700 million from Thursday's HK$266 million.
The yuan-based A share index lost 6.81 points, or 1.78 percent, to 375.20 on turnover of 3.4 billion yuan, unchanged from Thursday.
"The B index slid off its highs as a result of profit-taking after yesterday's surge," an analyst at Sun Hung Kai Investment Services Ltd said.
"There is still much room to rise next week," he said.

Analysts said the sharp rises on the B index, which closed on Thursday at its 10 percent limit-up, were fuelled by a flow of funds to the cheaper China B shares from Hong Kong's H shares -- shares of mainland firms issued in Hong Kong.
The index lost some strength in the afternoon because investors were cautious ahead of a three-day weekend, when many companies might release 1997 interim results, analysts said.
The Shenzhen stock exchange's B share market would close for one day on Monday, in line with a public holiday in Hong Kong.
"As we are entering the heat of the interim reporting season, an extra day of holiday posts a significant risk," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
China-listed companies must announce their 1997 first-half earnings by August 30, and only nine out of the 49 Shenzhen-listed B share firms have so far done so.
Rumours swirled the markets that Beijing may allow mainland Chinese to trade B shares, which are now limited to foreigners, after possibly permitting Sino-foreign investment funds.
Investors would be closely watching Luthai Textile Joint Stock Co Ltd, which would list 80 million B shares in Shnnzhen on Tuesday, for signs the markets have staged a real recovery, brokers said.

After a series of government measures to cool what seemed to be overheated stock markets in May, Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd became the first stock this year to fall through the offer price on its debut in July.
Analysts said Luthai, which had offered its share at HK$1.93, was poised for strong gains on Tuesday amid a feverish market. Long-term gains, however, may be capped by China's weak textile sector.
Bengang was the most actively traded share in the market with a volume of 38 million shares. It rose HK$0.16 to HK$2.75, compared with the HK$2.38 issue price.
In the A share market, property concern Shenzhen Worldsun Enterprises Ltd was the poorest performer, plunging to its 10 percent limit-down level of 10.15 yuan.
